researcher_notes: No defensible proposal year found. Dunkerque LNG has expressed a broad, undated FUTURE ambition to develop 'new molecules' business lines (CO2, hydrogen, ammonia imports/exports) leveraging its cold-management infrastructure - stated e.g. by its commercial director in April 2023 ('Nous devons developper... le role de Dunkerque LNG dans l'ecosysteme des nouvelles molecules (CO2, hydrogene, ammoniac...)', newsletterdunkerquelng.com/actu/415). But this is an aspirational strategy mention, not a distinct dated PROPOSAL/announcement of an ammonia import terminal. No press release, regulator filing, or FEED/open-season specifically announcing an ammonia import terminal at Dunkerque with an identifiable year could be verified; GEM's own record leaves the proposal year blank. Concrete Dunkerque decarbonisation projects that DID advance are CO2 (Air Liquide 'D'Artagnan'/CO2 export, 2024), not ammonia. Earliest defensible ammonia mention is 2022-2023 but too vague to tie to a proposal milestone. UNRESOLVED (ammonia is also out of GEM update scope per brief).

No construction-start year exists to find. 'Expansion 2' is the +2 mtpa (~+2.0 bcm/y) capacity increase from Elengy/Fosmax's 'Open Season Fos Cavaou 2021' (launched March 2021), offered for delivery 'from April 2030 until 2045 or beyond'. It is a capacity/regulatory-debottlenecking expansion planned to be developed 'as of 2030', with NO reported FID and NO physical groundbreaking/site works; Elengy's 2021-2024 activity was capacity auctions/subscriptions, not construction. (Expansion 1, the +to-10-mtpa debottlenecking, went operating in 2023.) GEM's own timeline leaves Expansion 2's construction year blank while carrying status 'construction'. Because no site works have been publicly reported and no source dates a construction start, there is no verifiable construction-start year. UNRESOLVED. Proposal year, if wanted, would be 2021 (open season launch), but the requested milestone here is construction-start.

No retirement year exists to find: the Puerto Brisa (Terminal Brisa, La Guajira/Dibulla) LNG import & regasification terminal was NEVER BUILT and never operated. It is a still-live PLANNED project (developer Energy Developments LLC with TransEnergy LNG; land lease signed 2021; Kogas-Tech engineering) that as of Nov 2024 was being described in the future tense ('construirán'/'they will build' - Forbes Colombia, verified 2024+Puerto Brisa). The GEM record's status 'retired' with substatus 'planned' is contradictory and appears to be a data anomaly: a project that never entered operation cannot have a retirement/decommission year. UNRESOLVED per brief guidance (never operated -> no defensible retirement year). Recommend flagging the retired+planned combination to the user for correction (likely should be proposed/planned, not retired). NOTE: distinct from the Puerto Brisa COAL terminal (built 2014, coal ops suspended 2017).

'retired / substatus planned' = a PLANNED (not-yet-happened) future retirement with NO real date. The BW Batangas is an INTERIM FSRU: FGEN's plan (since the 2019 pivot from onshore to offshore) has always been that the interim FSRU would eventually be REPLACED by a permanent onshore terminal, at which point the FSRU would be retired/demobilized. As of the latest available reporting the FSRU is still in service - it arrived Jun 2023, commissioned Sep 2023, received first cargo Oct 2023, and First Gen was granted a 25-year operating license in January 2025 - and no source gives a target year for retiring the interim FSRU or completing the permanent onshore facility. Per the shard hint, this is a planned retirement with no defensible year -> UNRESOLVED.
